title: One Reroll Allowed
statement: You roll a fair die and are paid its value in dollars. After seeing the first roll you may choose to reroll once, in which case you are paid the second roll instead. With optimal play, what is your expected payoff?
insight: Work backwards: a reroll is worth 3.5, so keep the first roll exactly when it beats 3.5.
redHerring: Averaging over strategies or trying to optimize both rolls at once.
hints: Start from the end. What is the second roll worth on average?
Compare each first roll with that value.
solution:
A reroll is worth $3.5$. Keep the first roll when it exceeds $3.5$, i.e. on 4, 5, 6.

$E = \tfrac{4+5+6}{6} + \tfrac36\cdot 3.5 = 2.5 + 1.75 = 4.25$.
